card.name: tong
card.notes: Fifth roster athlete (user, 2026-11-09: Tong.glb, an AI-rigged baby model, "do 1": a full-size fighter, the baby look a costume). Rigged by Scripts/rig_glb.py (the model's own 19-bone skin kept, renamed to Mixamo, arms straightened to Grandpa's rest) then Scripts/rig_mixamo.py at 1.75 m (x2.30 from 0.761 m). Card values picked by Claude (user gave none): quick and supple (speed 0.9 between Grandpa 0.75 and Kim 0.95, flexibility 1.0 like Kim), middling power (strength 0.65), a lighter neck than the adults (toughness 0.9, neck damage 0.045) and average stamina (0.04). The scan keeps a baby's proportions at adult size: a big head and short legs, so its own balance and reach. Strike mass scaled to body mass (3.0 kg per 78 kg). Same rules as grandpa.json otherwise.

style.summary: Balance: square and planted, knees softly bent, hands low (Mom's stance as the start; rebalanced at build time). Slap: a quick upward chop with a full hip and trunk turn (Mom's guess as the start; re-searched for Tong's body).

slap.note: (wind-up, strike, follow-through) degrees, slap_demo.py's conventions (see kim.json). Mom: quick, because every athlete drifts onto the podium ~0.75 s into stand targets and her slow joints (speed 0.7) need the time; a high arm (the face is ~30 cm above her shoulder) with a full trunk/hip turn and a lean, because her reach is short like Kim's (hand 17 cm short of the face in the best static pose vs Grandpa 4, Matt 1, Kim 16); the lead arm hangs at her side (in front it hit the podium in the wind-up); short follow-through.

card.length_ratio_note: A baby scan scaled to adult height (user 2026-11-09, option 1): thigh 0.18 H against the adult 0.20-0.28. The physics body follows the mesh, so Tong's legs are short on purpose.

sparring.note: Practice opponent: Grandpa's face from Tong's start pelvis (Mom's 0.72 m plus the 6 cm Tong's pelvis sits lower: 0.787 vs 0.847 m); up to 15 cm lower for Kim; leaning in when braced
